title: Work-energy theorem
caution: The sum is the net work done by all forces exerted on the object (3.2.A.4). Each force's work uses the displacement of the point at which that force is exerted (3.2.A.3); the force-times-distance form applies only where that force's parallel component is constant over the displacement.
ced_evidence: 3.2.A.4: "the change in an object's kinetic energy is equal to the sum of the work (net work) being done by all forces exerted on the object."
correction_note: product-owner-directed correction by the Claude session (David, 2026-10-10): the escalated row was corrected against its own CED evidence and re-checked by both independent checkers and the own-family veto

title: Potential energy of a system
body: A system composed of two or more objects has potential energy if the objects within that system only interact with each other through conservative forces. Potential energy is a scalar quantity associated with the position of objects within a system.
ced_evidence: 3.3.A.1: "has potential energy if the objects within that system only interact with each other through conservative forces"; 3.3.A.2: "scalar quantity associated with the position of objects within a system"
